cohort: The study involved 51 pregnancies among 37 patients (30 women, 7 men) who were either diagnosed with Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) during pregnancy or were receiving Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors (TKI) at the time of conception.
finding: Conception among CML patients while on TKI could be uncomplicated, and while patients may lose CML response following treatment interruption, nearly all regain response upon resuming therapy, making therapy during pregnancy rarely needed.
followup_time: Up to 48 months for maternal CML response post-delivery/abortion; infant outcomes assessed at birth.
